bad.title: Only the word Month up top
bad.text: Nothing in the top bar hints at a palette, so newcomers never learn it exists.

bad.title: Week numbers have no visible switch
bad.text: No button or menu turns them on, so people who don’t know the shortcut give up.

good.title: A Commands button with the shortcut
good.text: People can see the palette, and ⌘K or Ctrl+K on the button teaches the keys.

good.title: Show week numbers, first in the list
good.text: The command that hid behind a shortcut is now one click from the button.

good.title: Keys listed beside each command
good.text: Go to today shows T, so the palette teaches the faster way too.

bad.title: Change theme is the official name
bad.text: People think “dark mode”, not “theme”, so the right command sits unnoticed in the list.

bad.title: Just No results for dark mode
bad.text: Nothing points to Change theme, so people decide the app can’t go dark.
bad.wait: Type dark mode in the box to see this.

good.title: Matches “dark” under Change theme
good.text: The result says why it matched, so people learn the real name for next time.
good.wait: Type dark mode in the box to see this.

good.title: Letters in order count too
good.text: Typing thm still finds Change theme, so a rushed or partial word works.

bad.title: Sixteen one-word entries, A to Z
bad.text: Advanced, Misc and Tools say nothing about what they do, and nothing is grouped.

bad.title: Export or PDF, which one saves
bad.text: Both look right, and PDF only opens settings, so people try them one by one.

good.title: Export to PDF at the very top
good.text: It sits under Recent, so people who saved a PDF last time get it in one click.

good.title: Groups named File, View and Slide
good.text: People skip to the right group instead of reading every entry.

good.title: Every name is a verb and an object
good.text: Export as images and Print handouts say what happens before people click.

bad.title: Commands: / in the top bar
bad.text: The slash is a key people type every day, in and/or, dates and links.

bad.title: The palette opens mid-sentence
bad.text: Typing and/or pops it open, and the slash never reaches the note.
bad.wait: Type a / in the note to see this.

good.title: Commands on ⌘ K, like most apps
good.text: People already know the key from other apps, and it never clashes with typing.

good.title: The slash types like any key
good.text: People can write and/or in the note, and nothing pops up.

good.title: Opens only when people ask
good.text: Escape closes it and puts the cursor back where people were typing.
good.wait: Press Ctrl+K or ⌘K in the note to see this.

bad.title: Size M hides behind Filters
bad.text: Nothing on the button says a filter from an earlier visit is still on.

bad.title: No results for rain jacket
bad.text: Three rain jackets exist in other sizes, so people decide the shop has none.
bad.wait: Search for rain jacket to see this.

good.title: Size M stays in view as a chip
good.text: People see the leftover filter and can turn it off with one click.

good.title: The count names what’s left out
good.text: It says 3 more jackets come in other sizes, before people even search.

good.title: One click shows the other sizes
good.text: Show 3 in all sizes brings every match back without hunting for the filter.

bad.title: Under 30 min is quietly on
bad.text: Both lasagnas take 45 minutes or more, so even the right spelling finds nothing.

bad.title: No results, and nothing more
bad.text: It doesn’t repeat lasagne or hint at lasagna, so people can’t tell what went wrong.
bad.wait: Search for lasagne to see this.

good.title: It repeats what people typed
good.text: No quick recipes match “lasagne” lets people spot their own spelling.
good.wait: Search for lasagne to see this.

good.title: The close spelling is a button
good.text: Search for “lasagna” fixes the typo in one click, with no retyping.
good.wait: Search for lasagne to see this.

good.title: Then a way past the filter
good.text: Show 2 that take longer turns off Under 30 min for this search.
good.wait: Search for lasagne, then press Search for “lasagna” to see this.

bad.title: Fifteen checkboxes before any hotel
bad.text: Pool, Spa and Bar get the same space as price and breakfast, the two most people want.

bad.title: Under €120 is the last of 15
bad.text: The filter most people want first sits at the bottom of the grid.

bad.title: The hotels start below the grid
bad.text: People scroll past every checkbox before they see a single price.

good.title: Four chips, price first
good.text: Under €120, Breakfast, Free cancellation and Rating 8+ match how people pick a hotel.

good.title: The other eleven wait here
good.text: Pool, parking and the rest stay one click away without crowding the results.

good.title: Hotels in view right away
good.text: People see the list shrink as they tap each chip.

bad.title: Focus brings up nothing
bad.text: People have to type Golden hour and recall the spelling, though they played it this morning.

bad.title: Gol matches two songs
bad.text: Gold rush and Golden hour both show, so people still read and pick.
bad.wait: Type gol in the box to see this.

good.title: Focus alone opens the list
good.text: People don’t have to type a letter or remember how a name is spelled.

good.title: Golden hour first, before typing
good.text: Recently played puts this morning’s song one click away.
good.wait: Click the search box to see this.

good.title: Recent searches come back as chips
good.text: Clicking june lake or night runs an earlier search again.
good.wait: Click the search box to see this.

bad.title: Beneficiary entity, not who you pay
bad.text: Every label is the bank’s word, so people read all five and guess.

bad.title: Remittance information hides the message
bad.text: People looking for where March rent goes skip it, because the word means nothing to them.

bad.title: Each wrong guess is a click
bad.text: The demo has to explain each bank word, which is what the label should have done.
bad.wait: Click Beneficiary entity, then Value date, to see this.

good.title: A question people ask themselves
good.text: Who are you paying? matches the thought in their head, not a bank field.

good.title: Message for them, in plain words
good.text: People spot where March rent goes on the first try.

good.title: Found on the first try
good.text: The field fills in March rent, with no guessing on the way.
good.wait: Click Message for them to see this.

bad.title: Orbit holds the downloads
bad.text: Nothing in the name says offline, so people open Vibes, The Vault and Spark first.

bad.title: The Vault could mean anything
bad.text: Saved playlists, purchases or private files. People have to open it to find out.

bad.title: Every wrong guess adds a click
bad.text: People open sections one by one, and won’t remember which name meant what.
bad.wait: Open The Vault and Spark to see this.

good.title: Downloads says what’s inside
good.text: People looking for offline songs go there first.

good.title: Library for the saved playlists
good.text: A word people already use for their own collection.

good.title: Found in one click
good.text: The plain name gets people there on the first try.

bad.title: Add to basket, the first name
bad.text: People put the lamp in a basket.

bad.title: Cart in the top bar
bad.text: A second word, so people can’t be sure the lamp landed here.

bad.title: Then it opens as Your bag
bad.text: A third name for the same place, with Check out cart under it.

good.title: Add to basket, the only name
good.text: The word people read here is the word they’ll look for next.

good.title: Basket in the top bar
good.text: It matches the button, so people know where the lamp went.

good.title: Your basket, the same word
good.text: Check out basket follows, so the whole path reads as one place.

bad.title: Passport details hides under Payments
bad.text: People looking for a passport field rarely open a section about money.

bad.title: Account, where people look first
bad.text: It holds Profile, Password and Notifications, so the search dead-ends here.

good.title: 8 of 10 people chose Account
good.text: Watching where people click first showed which parent the label belongs under.

good.title: Account now holds the passport
good.text: The section people open first is the one with Passport details.

good.title: Passport details, right under Profile
good.text: Two clicks from the menu, in the place people already checked.
